## Illustrations and display

Topic `presentation`.

Fields: `illustrations` (`checkpoints`, `scenes`, `style`, `appearances`, `workflows`, `bundle`), `checkpoints[].illustrate`, `checkpoints[].effects.illustrations.workflows`, `chapters[].illustrations` (`style`, `appearances`), the lore line `Public appearance:`, `display.lore_names_public`, `display.continue_list` (with `group_card`, `chapter_card`, `wand`, `roll_chips`, `suggestions`), `effects.stage` (`schema.ts` `Story`, `StoryIllustrations`, `IllustrationLook`, `StoryDisplay`; `src/image/cast.ts`, `src/image/lore.ts`; `src/sprites/direction.ts` `readStageDirection`).

- **What it does.** `illustrations` asks for pictures of beats and scenes in one `style`, with each cast member's look in `appearances` (keyed by cast id). A beat's picture is cued by its `player_name`, or a neutral "establishing shot" when it has none; the internal `name` never reaches the image prompt. `checkpoints[].illustrate: false` skips the automatic beat and scene pictures while that beat is active (a picture the player asks for still runs). `chapters[].illustrations` overrides `style` and, per cast id, `appearances` while the active beat is in that chapter, so a costume can end with its act. Lore looks come from `Appearance:` lines in the story's scanned books, and only from an entry that has fired in this chat; a `Public appearance:` line is used whenever the scene mentions the entry, fired or not, and wins over `Appearance:`. A cast member whose roster `role` starts with narrator, storyteller, game master, GM, DM or system, or whose `view` is `omniscient`, is drawn only from the card's own appearance field, never from the card description; an authored appearance for a narrator is direction, not a body, so it never reaches the picture. A picture draws only who speaks in the recent messages or is named there (a cast member's full name or first name), never every enabled group member. The chat's opening picture is skipped when the start beat sets `effects.background` or `effects.stage` (the stage already shows the scene), the greeting is never drawn by the every-N cadence, and with no location fact yet the latest authored background on the path names the place. `display.lore_names_public: true` lets players see lore entry names in the inline timeline. `illustrations.workflows` maps a picture type (`scene`, `character`, `portrait`, `user`, `background`, `free`) to one of SillyTavern's ComfyUI workflow files (a name ending in `.json`); `checkpoints[].effects.illustrations.workflows` overrides it from that beat on, and the last beat on the path wins. It applies only on SillyTavern's ComfyUI source: the workflow is switched for that one picture, in memory, and the player's own selection comes back after it; a workflow the player lacks, or one without a `"%prompt%"` placeholder, falls back to their own and Setup says so. `illustrations.bundle` (`{ "<name>.json": { graph, sha256 } }`, sha256 of the compact JSON graph) carries the workflows for another install: Studio's Export with workflows fills it, and Install in SillyTavern adds one create-only (never over an existing name), after showing its node classes; a node that can run code, read files, or takes a path, folder, URL or file name input (other than `filename_prefix`) is never installed from a story, and custom nodes or models are never installed. The other `display` keys switch this story's presence items off: `continue_list` (its rows in Your stories), `group_card` (the card on its group's list icon), `chapter_card` (chapter title cards), `wand` (the wand-menu entries), `roll_chips` (the dice chips: every roll in Author view, and a `narrate: "public"` check's chip for players) and `suggestions` (the "What could I do?" button). Each defaults on and is edited in the Studio's Story tab under Story presence; an item shows only when both the story and the player's install-wide switch allow it, so a story can hide an item but never force one on. `effects.stage` (`{ framing: full | thigh | close, spotlight, cast: { <name>: { set, face, hidden } } }`) places sprites for a beat when the sprite stage is on.
- **Good.** A narrator appearance of "never drawn"; a style line shared by every picture; `"illustrate": false` on short connecting beats; a disguise in `Public appearance:` with the true form kept in `Appearance:`.
- **Bad.** A secret form in `appearances`, a `Public appearance:` line, or a background prompt that shows the twist: each leaks through the image prompt.
- **Local image batches.** With the local controller's warm cache, consecutive compatible image jobs keep their models in GPU memory. A text request reclaims that memory before replying; background text restoration waits through a one-minute image idle window. Memory pressure, a different workflow or model, and the Safe mode's evict setting can still require unloading. This is automatic and needs no story field.
- **Local text fitting.** If an automatic text-model layout loads but leaves too little free GPU memory, the controller retries once with a larger fitting target and remembers that correction for later loads. Context and desktop memory reserves stay unchanged; a second miss is reported as a refusal.
- **If wrong.** Public lore names spoil a story whose entry titles name the twist; leave `lore_names_public` off unless the titles are safe. A secret look in `Appearance:` still reaches the image prompt once its entry fires, so keep a form the player has not seen out of any entry that can fire before the reveal. A `set` or `face` in `effects.stage` that the character's installed sprites lack shows nothing new (diagnostic `stage-sprite-unknown`: "The stage cannot show this: the character has no installed sprite set or face by that name, so they keep the sprite they had."; checked against the packs the stage found for the open chat's cast).

The story's game panels have their own switches: `display.journal`, `display.stat_sheet` and `display.widgets` (see the next three topics).

<a id="visual-packs"></a>

## Visual packs

Topic `visual-packs`.

Fields: `illustrations.packs` (`packs.style`, `packs.identities`, `packs.places`, each binding `{ id, digest }`) (`schema.ts` `StoryVisualPacks`, `VisualPackRef`; `validate/illustrations.ts`; `src/sprites/packs/`).

- **What it does.** A visual pack is prepared art installed on this SillyTavern: an identity pack holds one character's accepted looks (a base image, an optional bust and expressions per look, the immutable visible traits and the image-model identity tags), a place pack holds one location's plate (with optional variants keyed by story state, such as `time_of_day: night`), and a style pack holds the shared visual target and per-model recipes. `illustrations.packs` binds them: `identities` maps a cast id to an identity pack, `places` maps a checkpoint id to a place pack (the last bound or backgrounded checkpoint on the chat's path wins, so a later beat with its own `effects.background` and no pack is an unbound place), and `style` names the style pack. Each binding names the pack `id` and its `digest` (the pack's sha256), so the chat plays exactly that revision: a newer install of the same pack is reported, never used, until the chat takes "Update to the latest" (the change is compatible, `visual-packs-changed`). Bindings are written by a pack export, not by hand; the Studio lists them and can remove one. One resolver reads them for every picture route: the sprite stage shows a bound look without any builder (a member with no sprite folder stands from the pack, and a look change switches to the pack's look when the pack has it), the prepared cast scene uses the bound look as its Qwen reference (with no builder it uses the install-wide scene recipe), and automatic pictures copy the identity tags verbatim and use the bound place's name and description; when every visible character (one or two) has a bound or accepted current look, an automatic scene picture is drawn from those reference images instead (setting `image.automaticRoute`, default auto), with the bound place's name, description and, where ComfyUI offers the input, its plate. Only the current look and the current place reach the image-prompt model, never another look, variant or place in the pack. Identity tags (`tagsByFamily`) and style recipes (`recipes`) are keyed by the image route's family id, `sdxl-illustrious` or `sdxl-noobai` (tags may add a `default` set); a short name such as `illustrious` or an unknown family refuses the whole pack with a problem naming the right id, so tags never fall back to `default` silently. Every pack file is checked against its sha256 before use; a missing pack, a changed file or a look the pack lacks falls back (the text route, the default look, or the authored background name) and the picture records which (`image_director.visual`).
- **Good.** Packs exported from the same preparation run as the installed sprites; one place pack per recurring location bound at the checkpoint where the party arrives; a style pack shared by every identity and place.
- **Bad.** A secret form in an identity pack's traits or tags (they reach every picture of that character); a hand-typed digest; binding a place pack to a checkpoint whose background shows somewhere else.
- **If wrong.** An unknown cast id or checkpoint id is refused at import; a binding whose pack is not installed, or whose digest no longer matches the installed pack, draws on the text route and records `pack-missing`; a changed file records `asset-mismatch`. Pictures and the cast scene placed while a pack or file changed mid-render are discarded.

<a id="quests"></a>

## Quests and milestones

Topic `quests`.

Fields: `quests[]` (`id`, `title`, `kind`, `visible_when`, `offered_when`, `done_when`, `failed_when`, `steps[]` with `text`, `done_when`, `failed_when`, `visible_when`, `progress`; `requires`, `progress`, `labels`, `giver`, `author_note`, `reward` with `set`, `effects`, `label`, `visible_when`; `promise`) and `milestones[]` (`id`, `title`, `when`, `secret`) (`engine/gameSchema.ts`, `engine/quests.ts`, `validate/quests.ts`).

- **What it does.** A side quest's status is computed from the blackboard every turn: hidden until `visible_when` holds; `offered` while `offered_when` holds and `visible_when` does not. `visible_when` is the acceptance: the quest turns active the moment it holds, so an offered quest needs one, and an offered quest never fails, so the player may ignore it. Active, then done when `done_when` holds or failed when `failed_when` holds; when both hold at one boundary, failed wins. The end is kept: the story latches it in `quest_<id>_closed`, so a completion gate that turns false again does not reopen the quest, while a swipe or edit of the reply that closed it does. `done_when` may be left out: it is then every step done, or `progress` reaching its target (`{quality, of}`, drawn as N/M). `requires: [questId]` adds "that quest is done" (its `quest_<id>_closed` latch, so a failed prerequisite never opens it and a done one stays done) to this one's `visible_when` (and `offered_when`); a cycle is refused. `labels` words the end for players ("Left behind" instead of "Failed"). `giver` names a roster id; `author_note` is never shown to players. While a quest is hidden its `visible_when` keys are read by extraction; while active, its `done_when`, `failed_when` and open steps (`QUEST_SCOPE_CAP` keys at most: active quests first, then offered, then hidden, and inside each every quest's first key before any quest's second, so a quest is never starved by a busier one; when active quests would fill every slot, one is kept for an offered or hidden quest's keys, taken in turn, so a quest waiting to be found is still read; the rest are named in Author view's setup list). A reward lands once, when the quest is done: `set` writes code qualities (a literal or `{add: n}`; an add on a stepped quality, such as a relationship, stays inside its step bounds), `effects` switches `world_info`, `cast_changes` and `npc_replies` (trigger `onEnter`), and a swipe or edit of the reply that earned it takes all of it back. `reward.label` shows the reward to players, behind `reward.visible_when`. The main line is the checkpoint graph: the reached beats' `player_name`s and the active beat's `player_text`. A milestone is earned when `when` holds; a `secret` one is not listed until it is earned. The Journal, the log, `/story quests`, the welcome-back recap and the inline chips "Quest started / completed / failed" show only visible quests and steps.
- **Promises.** The story remembers a promise the player makes to one cast member in the player's exact words (Promises remembered, on by default): the read writes it only when a line the player wrote commits them to that member, with no hedge, refusal, question, sarcasm or quoted speech, and only that member's private prompt carries the reminder, when the scene touches it. An undated promise stays open; a deadline is kept only when the player's words agree one, and a passed deadline never counts as broken. Kept, broken, changed and released are recorded from evidence words, and a swipe or edit takes them back. The player sees their open promises on This story → Play as their own quoted words. A foreseen promise belongs in a quest: `promise: true` with a `giver` links a promise the player makes to that giver in the quest's words (its title and step texts) to the quest, and the quest's done or failed state becomes the promise's, so it is never tracked twice. A promise quest without a `giver` is refused.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "find-the-map", "title": "The cartographer's map", "visible_when": { "q": "met_cartographer", "op": "==", "v": true }, "steps": [{ "text": "Find the cartographer's lodgings", "done_when": { "q": "found_lodgings", "op": "==", "v": true } }, { "text": "Bring back the map", "done_when": { "q": "has_map", "op": "==", "v": true } }], "reward": { "label": "A safe road east", "effects": { "world_info": { "enable": [{ "lorebook": "Ruins Lore", "comments": ["Map routes"] }] } } } }`.
- **Bad.** A reward on a quest that is done before anything happens (refused); `done_when` and `failed_when` that both hold at the start (refused); an offered quest that fails on time alone (`messages_in_checkpoint`, refused); a step title that names a later beat.
- **Story updates.** Editing a quest keeps what this chat reached. A changed reward that this chat already received is not given again; removing a quest this chat finished or failed asks whether to keep the chat or restart; removing an active one just stops tracking it.
- **If wrong.** A quest whose keys no transition reads is still discovered: its keys are in the read while it is hidden or active. A quest whose `visible_when` never holds never shows; Author view lists it as not found yet.

<a id="checks"></a>

## Checks

Topic `checks`.

Fields: `checkpoints[].checks[]` and `transitions[].check` (`id`, `label`, `quality`, `roll` with `sides`, `target`, `dice`; `modifiers[]` with `q`, `v`, `add`, `label`, `hint`; `narrate`, `outcome` with `quality`, `bands`, `partial_margin`; `twist`; `when`, checkpoint checks only; `hint_when`) (`engine/storyChecks.ts`, `validate/checks.ts`, `validate/checkRefs.ts`, `runtime/storyCheckDraws.ts`, `runtime/suggestionAnchors.ts`).

- **What it does.** A check rolls seeded dice once per visit to its checkpoint (the transition's `from`): the draw is keyed by the chat, the story, the boundary the checkpoint started at and `check:<id>:<die>`, so group replies, a swipe and a reopened chat see the same roll, and a re-entry rolls again. The total is the dice plus every `modifiers` row whose quality holds its value, read each turn: finding the rope can turn a miss into a success, asking again cannot. It writes `quality` (a code bool, true at or above `target`); `outcome` also writes a code enum of exactly `miss`, `weak` and `strong` (weak below `target + partial_margin`); `twist: {quality}` writes true when two or more dice match. A transition check is attempted when the rest of its gate holds; a checkpoint check when the checkpoint is reached, or, with `when` (an ordinary gate), at the first turn of the visit where `when` holds. Until then it is pending and writes nothing; it then rolls once for that visit, with the same seeded dice and the modifiers that hold at that turn, and keeps that outcome for the rest of the visit even if `when` turns false or a modifier changes. The story keeps the turn it rolled at in `check_<id>_rolled` (reserved), so a swipe or edit of the reply that rolled takes the roll back and the replay rolls the same dice, and a re-entry is pending again. `when` must name declared qualities (an unknown key is refused with the nearest one) and must not read what the check writes; its extracted keys are read while the checkpoint is active, and so are the keys of `hint_when` and every `modifiers` row (for a transition check, while its `from` is active), so a quality used only by a check is still asked about there and nowhere else; it needs no `state_snapshot` entry; a transition check takes no `when`. Each attempt with a new outcome is recorded, and the next reply is told the outcome (never the dice). `narrate: "public"` also shows the roll under the message, "Climb: 15 + 4 vs 12, success"; `hidden` (the default) shows only what the story tells, and the roll only in Author view.
- **What could help.** On a public check, a modifier may carry a `hint`: the player's words for the help, at most 60 characters ("a rope"). While the check waits for the attempt (a transition check whose gate's other conditions do not hold yet, or a checkpoint check with `when` that has not rolled this visit), What could I do? shows one line, "Climb — could help: a rope, a friend's hand", and may build a suggestion on it. It lists every hint of a modifier that adds, in the order written, whatever the dice and whether the modifier holds; a modifier whose quality is public adds "(you have it)" while it holds, a hidden one never shows its state. Never the dice, the target, the faces or whether it would succeed. `hint_when` (a gate, declared keys, not what the check writes) limits when the list shows. A hint on a hidden check is refused. A hint naming a place, quest or person the player may not have met warns (`check-hint-names-unknown`: "The help is held back while it names a place, quest or person the player has not met, so it may never show."), and at play every hint is checked against what the player knows and the secrets held from them before it shows.
- **Good.** `"check": { "id": "climb", "label": "Climb", "quality": "climb_ok", "roll": { "sides": 20, "target": 12 }, "modifiers": [{ "q": "has_rope", "v": true, "add": 4, "label": "Rope" }], "narrate": "public" }` on `wall → rooftops`, gated on `tried_climb == true` and `climb_ok == true`. A checkpoint check that waits for the party to try: `"checks": [{ "id": "climb", "quality": "climb_ok", "roll": { "sides": 20, "target": 12 }, "when": { "q": "tried_climb", "op": "==", "v": true }, "narrate": "public" }]`.
- **Bad.** A latching or extracted check quality (refused: the roll writes it every turn); two checks writing one quality (refused); a check on a generated beat (refused).
- **If wrong.** A gate that waits only on the check quality fires the moment the checkpoint starts; pair it with a quality the player's attempt sets. A pending check keeps its qualities' last values (the start value on a first visit, the last roll on a re-entry), so a route reading them still needs the attempt too.

<a id="offers"></a>

## Offers

Topic `offers`.

Fields: `checkpoints[].offers[]` (`id`, `text`, `visible_when`, `needs` with `when`, `reason`) (`engine/offerSchema.ts`, `validate/offers.ts`, `runtime/suggestionAnchors.ts`, `studio/offerDiagnostics.ts`).

- **What it does.** An offer is a line the player could say or do at one beat, written by you, like a clue's `action`: at most 8 a checkpoint, `text` at most 200 characters. While its checkpoint is active and `visible_when` holds (or has none), What could I do? may build one of its suggestions on it, and if the model leaves it out the offer is listed as you wrote it; picking it only fills the box where the player types. With `needs: {when, reason}`, an offer whose `when` does not hold yet is shown greyed with your `reason` ("You need a lantern first", at most 120 characters) and cannot be picked; greyed offers show in Author view only (owner 2026-10-25), and the player sees only the offers that are open. Nothing is ever generated from the story's transitions, gates or checkpoint names, so greying never shows a hidden route. Each suggestion builds on at most three things the player already knows, picked in code: the current task, an open quest step, an open or older thread, a promise the player made, a clue's action, a check's help line, an offer or a story pattern about to complete.
- **Good.** `"offers": [{ "id": "ask-toll", "text": "I ask the ferryman what the crossing costs." }, { "id": "go-below", "text": "I light the lantern and go below deck.", "needs": { "when": { "q": "has_lantern", "op": "==", "v": true }, "reason": "You need a lantern first." } }]`.
- **Bad.** `needs` reading a check's result, its roll turn or a latch (refused: the grey row would tell the player a hidden outcome); an offer naming a checkpoint, quest or person the player has not reached or met (`offer-names-unknown`: "The offer is held back while it names a place, quest or person the player has not met, so it may never show."). At play every offer's text and reason is checked against the names the player knows and the secrets held from them before it shows.
- **Story updates.** Offers are presentation: editing them is compatible and shows at the next open of the panel. Nothing about them is stored in the chat.

<a id="widgets"></a>

## Stats and story panels

Topic `widgets`.

Fields: `qualities[].display` (`public`, `label`, `as`, `group`, `min`, `max`, `bands`, `hide_when_empty`, `trend`), `widgets[]` (`id`, `kind`, `title`, `bind`, `options`, `visible_when`, `audience`, `accent`, `icon`, `rows[]`, `dates`, `actions[]` with `id`, `text`, `open`, `check`), `display.journal`, `display.stat_sheet`, `display.widgets`, `display.motion`, `display.standing` (`engine/gameSchema.ts`, `validate/display.ts`, `validate/widgets.ts`, `runtime/widgets.ts`, `runtime/widgetHistory.ts`).

- **What it does.** `display: {public: true, label, as}` puts a quality on the player's Stat sheet: `item` (a bool, shown once true, grouped as Inventory), `count`, `meter` (a number with `min` and `max`), `boxes` (an int at most 12 apart) or `word` (an enum with `player_labels`, or a bounded number with `bands: [{max, label}, …, {label}]`, ascending, the last open). A number with both `min` and `max` keeps them as its range: every write (the reader, a quest reward, a faction move) is clamped into it on the blackboard, so what the player sees is the stored value. `hide_when_empty` (default on for items and counts) keeps an empty row out; `trend` adds an arrow against the previous turn. Nothing that is not public is ever sent to a panel. A widget is a closed panel bound by reference: `meters` (`"quality:<key>"`, `{qualities}` or `{group}`), `track` (`"path"` or `"quests"`), `log`, `clock` (one int whose `min` and `max` are 2 to 12 apart; it clamps, and "full" is an ordinary gate), `board` (`"quests"` or `"arcs"`, read-only lanes), `roster` and `timeline`; `clues` and `map` carry their own items (next section), `html` is a story-made page over another widget's view (the section after) and `scene` is the where-when-who card (its own section). A `roster` lists `rows: [{id, member | label, quality | faction, when?}]`: a party or a set of factions, each named by a roster id (shown as the card name) or a `label`, with the status word of an enum quality (public, with `player_labels`, on a player widget) or, with `faction`, that faction's band word while it is visible (never a number, never "changed … ago"), and a row with `when` shows only while its gate holds. `display.standing: false` keeps the Standing group off the Stat sheet. A `timeline` lists the checkpoints the chat has reached that have a `player_name`, in the order first reached, under their chapter's player title when the story has `chapters`, with an optional authored date per checkpoint (`dates: {"<checkpoint id>": "Day 3"}`); the active one is marked "you are here" and one reached at the last turn is marked new. A meter, a clock box and a roster row say when what the player sees last changed ("changed 2 replies ago"), counted from the turns this chat keeps; a value that moved past what the meter shows is not a change. In Author view each panel also lists, per value, the quality key, who last wrote it (the reader, the story's own code, or you) and the message and boundary. Any widget may carry `actions` (at most 10), buttons under the panel: a plain one puts its `text` in the box where the player types (never sent); `open: "overview" | "memory"` opens This story → Play (at What the story remembers for `memory`); `check: "<id>"` names a public transition check, shows its dice ("Climb: d20 vs 12") and puts the attempt line in the box, and shows only while that check is waiting for the attempt at the current checkpoint. `display.motion: false` turns the panels' transitions off for this story (they are off anyway when the player's system asks for reduced motion). With no widget the Journal is a track and a log, and the Stat sheet is every public quality; an authored widget of the same kind replaces it. `audience: "author"` shows a widget in Author view only; an author `meters` widget may bind a quality with no `display`, shown by its key and raw value. `accent` and `icon` come from a fixed list; there is no markup.
- **Good.** `{ "key": "supplies", "type": "int", "source": "extractor", "rubric": "…", "display": { "public": true, "label": "Supplies", "as": "meter", "min": 0, "max": 10, "bands": [{ "max": 2, "label": "Running out" }, { "max": 6, "label": "Enough" }, { "label": "Well stocked" }] } }`.
- **Bad.** `display` on a relationship (`rel_*`) or on a key a checkpoint-gated World Info entry names (refused: it would spoil); a player widget bound to a quality that is not public (refused); a clock bound to a pressure pool (not built yet); a roster row on a quality that is not an enum, or on a hidden one in a player widget (refused); an action on a hidden check, or on a checkpoint's own check, which rolls by itself (refused); an action that opens an Author view tab (refused).
- **If wrong.** An empty group or section is never drawn, and counts come only from what shows, so a panel never hints at hidden rows.

<a id="clues-and-maps"></a>

## Clue walls and maps

Topic `clues-and-maps`.

Fields: `widgets[].clues[]` (`id`, `text`, `quality` or `when`, `action`), `widgets[].links[]` (`from`, `to`, `label`), `widgets[].image`, `widgets[].pins[]` (`id`, `label`, `x`, `y`, `checkpoint` or `when`, `action`) (`engine/gameSchema.ts`, `validate/widgets.ts`, `runtime/widgets.ts`, `studio/widgetDiagnostics.ts`).

- **What it does.** A `clues` widget is a wall of what the player has found. Each clue shows once its bool `quality` is true or its `when` gate holds; until then it is not sent to the panel at all, not even hidden, and the wall never says how many are left. A link shows once both of its clues show. A `map` widget is a picture with pins: `image` is the file name of a SillyTavern background (the picture is served by SillyTavern itself, never from a link), and each pin sits at `x`, `y`, a percentage of the picture's width and height. A pin with a `checkpoint` shows once the story has reached that checkpoint and marks "you are here" while it is the active one; a pin with `when` shows while its gate holds (use a latching bool for "visited"). A clue or a pin may carry an `action`: the player's own line, which a button puts in the box where they type, to send or change; nothing is sent and no story value is written by the panel. The panel's own `actions` (see Stats and story panels) add buttons that open This story → Play or ask for a public check. A clue or pin that appeared at the last turn is marked new (and slides in, unless the player's system asks for reduced motion). A panel never adds anything to what the reading model is asked, so gate clues and pins on qualities the story already reads.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "wall", "kind": "clues", "title": "Clue wall", "clues": [{ "id": "ledger", "text": "A torn ledger page, signed M.", "quality": "found_ledger", "action": "I show the ledger page to the ferryman." }, { "id": "boots", "text": "Wet boot prints to the boathouse.", "when": { "q": "searched_dock", "op": "==", "v": true } }], "links": [{ "from": "ledger", "to": "boots", "label": "same night" }] }`; `{ "id": "river", "kind": "map", "title": "The river", "image": "river-map.jpg", "pins": [{ "id": "landing", "label": "The landing", "x": 18, "y": 70, "checkpoint": "start" }] }`.
- **Bad.** A clue gated on a quality nothing else reads (`widget-item-never-read`: it stays at its start value, so the clue never shows); a pin on a checkpoint no path reaches (`map-pin-unreachable`); an `image` that is a link or a path (refused) or a file the install does not have (`map-image-missing`); a clue's `text` that names a secret before the clue is found would reveal (the text shows the moment it is found, so write it as what the player sees).
- **If wrong.** A wall with nothing found yet is not drawn; a map with no pin reached still shows its picture. A clue found in a reply shows at the next reply: the reading runs after the reply and lands at the next boundary, like every reading. An author's `/cp set` of a clue's quality holds against a reading of the messages it already saw; only evidence from a later message changes it again. The Studio checks a clue written with `quality` exactly like one with `when` (`widget-item-never-read`).

<a id="html-panels"></a>

## Story-made HTML panels

Topic `html-panels`.

Fields: `widgets[].template`, `widgets[].source`, `widgets[].actions[]` (`id`, `text`), the page's `window.storyWidget` (`ready`, `onData`, `propose`, `resize`) (`runtime/htmlWidget.ts`, `components/widgets/HtmlWidgetFrame.tsx`).

- **What it does.** An `html` widget is a page the story brings for a layout the other kinds cannot draw. `source` names an ordinary widget of the story; the page is shown that widget's player view and nothing else, and that widget is what the player sees instead when they switch "Story-made panels" off. The page runs in a sandboxed frame with no same-origin access and a content policy that blocks every network request, so it cannot reach SillyTavern, the chats, the settings, cookies or storage, and cannot fetch or load anything from outside (pictures must be inline `data:` URLs). It talks to the extension only through a small message bridge: `window.storyWidget.onData(render)` receives the view (and every later change), `ready()` starts it, `propose(id)` asks to put the matching `actions` line in the box where the player types (never sent; refused while the player is typing, and at most one every 1.5 s), or, for an action with `open`, to open This story → Play, and `resize()` asks for the frame's height. `ready()` answers with `hostContext.motion` (`"off"` when the story turned motion off). Any other message is refused. Every message is kept in the page's bridge log (`storyOrchestratorWidgetBridge.audit()`), and the opening, each action and each refusal go into the session journal. A page that opens another page after it loaded is closed at once and its plain panel shows. The view and every later change reach a page only after its own `ready()` finished, so a page that leaves while it is still loading never gets them (the frame shows wherever it went). No content policy can stop a page from opening an address itself, so a page could carry what it was shown away in that address before the panel closes: read the template of a story you did not write. The Studio lists every HTML panel under Diagnostics (`html-widget-declared`) so the template is read before the story is shared.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "wall-page", "kind": "html", "title": "Case board", "source": "wall", "actions": [{ "id": "ask", "text": "I ask the ferryman about the ledger." }], "template": "<div id=b></div><script>storyWidget.onData(function(w){document.getElementById('b').replaceChildren(w.body.clues.map(function(c){return c.text}).join(' / '))});storyWidget.ready();</script>" }`.
- **Bad.** A template that loads a script, a font or a picture from a link (blocked, so it renders without it); a `source` that is another HTML panel or shown to a different audience (refused); a template that hides spoilers in its own text and waits to reveal them (the text ships with the story, so anyone can read it; reveal only what the view says).
- **If wrong.** With "Story-made panels" off, or on a browser that blocks the frame, the player gets the `source` panel, so the story never depends on the page.

<a id="widget-scene"></a>

## Scene card

Topic `widget-scene`.

Fields: `widgets[]` with `kind scene` (`kind: "scene"`), `options.time`, `options.standing` (`engine/gameSchema.ts`, `validate/widgets.ts`, `runtime/sceneCard.ts`, `components/widgets/WidgetCard.tsx`).

- **What it does.** A `scene` widget is a small player card that answers where, when and with whom. "Where" is the location the Overview already shows (the scene tracker's place, in its `player_labels` word). "When" shows only with `options.time: true` on a story with a clock (the same label as the timeline); without it, or without a clock, there is no time line. "With you" lists the enabled cast members who are not away by their schedule, and only those the player has met: a member with its own People entry shows once that entry is known, a member without one shows while enabled, and a narrator-type member (`view: "omniscient"`, or a narrator role) is never listed. Each name shows the card's portrait (initials when the card has none) and links to its People page when it has one. A member the player has not met is not on the card at all: no name, no picture, no initials, no count. "With you" means in the scene's cast (enabled, not away); it is not proof of being seen in the room. Nothing is placed for you: the card shows only in a story that declares a `scene` widget. Under each name come the lines the player already has elsewhere: the member's relationship labels (the same lines as its People page), only those toward you or toward someone else on the card, a secret label only once its reveal has happened (it then reads "Learned: …"); and, with `options.standing: true`, the band word of each group (faction) the member belongs to, while that group is visible ("The Guild: Wary", the same word as the Standing sheet). Standing is off unless you ask for it because it shows who belongs to which group: leave it off when a member's allegiance is meant to be a surprise. The card never says when a line changed and shows no trend.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "here", "kind": "scene", "title": "Here now", "options": { "time": true, "standing": true } }` in a story with a clock, People pages, labelled relationships and factions.
- **Bad.** `options.time` or `options.standing` on any other kind (refused); `options.standing` in a story where a member secretly works for a visible group (the card would say so); expecting the card to name someone the player has not met (it never does: give the member a People entry with `known_when` to control when they appear).
- **If wrong.** An empty card (no location yet, no time, nobody met) is not drawn. A member who leaves by a cast change or a schedule leaves the card at the next reply.

<a id="display-narrate"></a>

## The sheet reaches the narrator

Topic `display-narrate`.

Fields: `qualities[].display.narrate` (`display.narrate`: `"omniscient"` or `false`) (`engine/gameSchema.ts`, `validate/display.ts`, `runtime/narratorSheet.ts`, `runtime/narratorSheetPort.ts`).

- **What it does.** A public quality is shown to the player on the Stat sheet; with `display.narrate` (default `"omniscient"`) the same line, in the player's own words (the item name, the count, the band word, never a hidden number), also goes to the narrator: only into the private block of members with `view: "omniscient"`, on their own drafted turns, so the narrator does not deny an item the sheet shows or invent one it does not. Other characters never get it: what the player sees is not something every character knows. The narrator also gets "just happened" lines for the boundaries since its last request: visible quest moves, earned milestones (never a secret one) and band changes of narrated meters; they ride every request until the next boundary commits, a turn with no reply carries them to the next request, at most six lines, and a swipe or rollback takes them back with the boundary. `false` keeps a quality out. A story with no narrated public quality sends nothing new. Like every private block it is withheld from quiet and impersonate requests. The check-outcome block also says: narrate only the outcomes and consequences listed; a failure means the attempt did not succeed, with no added costs.
- **Good.** `"display": { "public": true, "label": "Lantern", "as": "item" }` with a narrator member `{ "id": "narrator", "view": "omniscient" }`: the narrator sees "Inventory: Lantern" once the player has it.
- **Bad.** `"narrate": "everyone"` (refused: the sheet reaches the narrator only, because a player-visible item acquired in private is not known to every character); a story with no omniscient member (nothing reaches anyone; add a narrator member or leave it).
- **If wrong.** A line changes only when the shown value changes, so the block stays the same turn after turn. Hide a quality from the narrator with `"narrate": false`, not by making it non-public.

<a id="display-warn"></a>

## Warning bands

Topic `display-warn`.

Fields: `qualities[].display.bands[].warn` (`bands[].warn`) (`engine/gameSchema.ts` `DisplayBand`, `validate/display.ts`, `runtime/gameSheet.ts`).

- **What it does.** A band of a public meter may carry `warn` (at most 80 characters). While the value sits in that band the Stat sheet shows the line as a chip under the meter, and the narrator (see the topic above) gets the same line. It never shows a number.
- **Good.** `"bands": [{ "max": 2, "label": "Dying", "warn": "One more wound could kill you." }, { "max": 6, "label": "Hurt" }, { "label": "Fine" }]`.
- **Bad.** `warn` on a faction band (refused: standing shows only its band word); a warning on a relationship (relationships are never public); a line longer than 80 characters (refused).
- **If wrong.** The chip follows the stored value, so it appears and leaves with the band at the next reply.

<a id="codex"></a>

## People and Places

Topic `codex`.

Fields: `codex` (`people[]`, `places[]`; each entry `id`, `name`, `member`, `location`, `aliases`, `known_when`, `facts[]` with `id`, `text`, `known_when`, `source`, `rev`), `display.codex` (`engine/codexSchema.ts`, `engine/codex.ts`, `validate/codex.ts`, `runtime/codexView.ts`, `components/codex/CodexPage.tsx`).

- **What it does.** The Journal gains a People page and a Places page that fill in as the player learns. A person names a roster `member` (shown by the card name) or a free `name` for someone who never appears; a place has a `name` and may name a `location` value of the story's `location` enum, and is then known once the party has been there. Each fact's `known_when` is a gate, `{"reached": "<checkpoint id>"}` (the chat has reached that checkpoint) or `"start"` (the player knows it from the opening: their background, the first place). An entry's own `known_when` makes it appear before any fact does (a person met, a place visited). A line latches the first turn its condition holds and stays, so a later change never takes it away; only a swipe, edit or delete of the reply that earned it does. Until then nothing about it is sent to the page, not even a hidden row, and the page counts only what shows: an entry with nothing known is absent, and a page with no entry has no tab. A fact may name a `source` (an entry or roster id); "From <name>" shows under it once that source is itself known, and a `reached` fact says "At <place>" from the checkpoint's player name. A fact learned at the last turn is marked new, and the log says "Learned about <name>". `aliases` are other names for the entry, used to keep an unmet name out of suggestions. The story reads every key a codex gate names while the entry or fact is unknown (people and places not yet known first, `DISCOVERY_SCOPE_CAP` keys a read, the rest taking turns), so a codex gate needs no transition to be read. Telling the player a fact gives no character that knowledge. `display.codex: false` hides both pages for this story. Ids are lowercase letters, digits and `-`; at most 12 facts an entry, text up to 200 characters, plain (no macros).
- **Good.** `"codex": { "people": [{ "id": "ferryman", "member": "tom", "facts": [{ "id": "job", "text": "Runs the night crossing.", "known_when": { "reached": "landing" } }, { "id": "debt", "text": "Owes money to someone upriver.", "known_when": { "q": "heard_debt", "op": "==", "v": true }, "source": "innkeeper" }] }], "places": [{ "id": "boathouse", "name": "The boathouse", "location": "boathouse", "facts": [{ "id": "door", "text": "The back door does not lock.", "known_when": { "q": "searched_dock", "op": "==", "v": true } }] }] }`. Facts describe something that stays true ("Owes money upriver"), not a scene event ("Shouted at you on the pier").
- **Bad.** A fact under an early gate that names the twist, or names a person the player has not met yet (`disclosure-names-unknown-entity`: the text shows the moment the fact is known); a fact that waits for a checkpoint no path reaches or a value nothing writes (`codex-fact-never-read`); a gate that already holds at the start (`codex-gate-holds-at-start`: mark it `"start"` instead); a `reached` checkpoint that does not exist, two entries with one id, or two person pages for one member (refused).
- **Story updates.** Rewording a fact's `text` (same `known_when`, same `rev`) is a correction: a chat that knows it sees the new words at once. Changing its `known_when`, or raising its `rev`, makes it a new discovery: a chat that knew the old one loses it and learns the new one when its condition holds. Removing an entry or a fact drops what a chat learned of it.
- **If wrong.** A fact read in a reply shows at the next reply, like every reading. When the read is crowded, Author view's setup list says which codex keys wait a turn (`discovery-scope-overflow`).

<a id="codex-returns"></a>

## Return visits

Topic `codex-returns`.

Fields: `places[].returns[]` (`id`, `text`, `when`, `rev`) (`engine/codexSchema.ts`, `engine/codex.ts`, `validate/codex.ts`, `runtime/codexView.ts`).

- **What it does.** A place with a `location` may carry up to 6 `returns`: lines that acknowledge something that happened there, shown when the party comes back. A return waits until the place is known and its `when` (a gate or `{"reached": "<checkpoint id>"}`, never `"start"`) holds while the party is somewhere else; the next time the party's `location` is that place, the line shows on the place page, marked new for that turn. An event that happens while the party is still there shows nothing until the party leaves and comes back, and a first visit is never a return. Return lines are page-side only: nothing is sent to a model (an in-world reminder for the narrator stays authored checkpoint `world_info`). A swipe of the reply that brought the party back takes the line away, and the return shows again on the replayed turn.
- **Good.** `"returns": [{ "id": "door", "text": "The back door still hangs off one hinge.", "when": { "q": "dock_fight", "op": "==", "v": true } }]`.
- **Bad.** A return on a person, on a place without `location`, or with `"start"` is refused; its text follows the fact rules (`disclosure-names-unknown-entity`, `codex-fact-never-read`).
- **Story updates.** Rewording a return keeps it shown; changing its `when` or raising its `rev` makes the chat come back for it again.

<a id="observations"></a>

## Things the player notices

Topic `observations`.

Fields: `observations[]` (`id`, `text`, `when`, `source`, `rev`, `passive` with `roll` and `modifiers`), `display.observations` (`engine/observationSchema.ts`, `engine/observations.ts`, `validate/observations.ts`, `runtime/observationRecords.ts`, `runtime/observationView.ts`).

- **What it does.** An observation is a small authored detail the player can notice: "The lock has fresh scratches." It shows once its `when` holds (a gate or `{"reached": "<checkpoint id>"}`; never `"start"`: a line known from the opening is a codex fact). The first turn it holds it latches as `obs_<id>` and stays; only a swipe, edit or delete of the reply that earned it takes it back. That turn the story card says "You notice: …" (at most 3 lines, then "and N more in the Journal"), and the Journal keeps it under **Noticed**, newest first, with "From <name>" once its `source` (a codex entry or roster id) is known, "At <place>" for a `reached` line, and a link back to the reply. With `passive` the player may not notice it at all: the first turn `when` holds the story rolls once, seeded by the chat, the story, that turn and the line (`roll {sides, target, dice}` plus `modifiers` that add when a quality has a value, as for checks), and nobody sees the roll. A success notices it; a miss is final (`obs_<id>_missed`), so repeating the move never fishes for it. An observation gated on another latch (a codex line, a label reveal, a quest close) lands one turn later on a turn without a transition, and the same turn when a transition fires. Page only: nothing about it is sent to any model, no character learns it, and the narrator is not told. The page shows a line only while it names no one the player has not met and restates no secret the story keeps from the player. While a line is unnoticed (not yet noticed or missed), the keys its gate and its `modifiers` read are read for you in turn with the codex, so a quality used only as a modifier needs no `state_snapshot` entry. `display.observations: false` hides the card line and the section. At most 60 a story; text up to 200 characters, plain (no macros); ids are lowercase letters, digits and `-`.
- **Good.** `"observations": [{ "id": "scratches", "text": "Fresh scratches circle the lock of the dock shed.", "when": { "q": "searched_dock", "op": "==", "v": true } }, { "id": "pitch", "text": "A faint smell of pitch hangs in the air.", "when": { "reached": "boathouse" }, "passive": { "roll": { "sides": 20, "target": 12 } } }]`. Write what is there to see, hear or smell.
- **Bad.** A line that tells the player what they feel, think, realise or suspect ("You sense he is lying": `observation-imposes-mind`), or what to do ("You should check the boat": `observation-instructs`); a line naming someone the player may not know yet (`disclosure-names-unknown-entity`); a gate on a checkpoint no path reaches or a value nothing writes (`observation-never-read`); a gate that holds before anything happens (`observation-gate-holds-at-start`). The wording checks are warnings: read the line again rather than fight the checker. A gate on the line's own `obs_` key, an unknown checkpoint or quality, an unknown `source`, two lines with one id, or an authored quality starting `obs_` is refused.
- **Story updates.** Rewording `text` (same `when`, `passive` and `rev`) is a correction: a chat that noticed it sees the new words. Changing `when` or `passive`, or raising `rev`, makes it a new discovery: the chat loses the old one (and a miss) and notices the new one when its moment comes. Removing it drops it from the chat.
- **If wrong.** A line gated on something read in a reply shows at the next reply, like every reading. Author view shows each passive roll as a chip under the reply.
